rules.message: Full cover needs an Eligible Household (BPL) card under NFSA 2013 or RSBY enrolment; other residents get co-payment cover

benefits.text: Eligible Households (BPL) and RSBY beneficiaries: cover of up to ₹5,00,000 per family per year.
Other residents (not Eligible Households): the scheme pays 30% of the package rate, up to ₹1.5 lakh per family per year; the patient pays the remaining 70%.
Covers simple secondary, complex secondary, tertiary and emergency procedures.

required_documents.name: Food (ration) card - BPL or APL card
For children: child's birth certificate and parents' Aadhaar cards

how_to_apply.text: Go to the nearest Public Health Institution (PHI) with Aadhaar and ration card, enrol and get the AB-ArK card.
Get diagnosed at the PHI. If the PHI cannot treat the illness, it gives a referral letter for treatment at any empanelled government or private hospital.
In an emergency, go directly to any empanelled hospital without a referral.

evidence.claim: All residents of Karnataka; integrated with Ayushman Bharat
evidence.quote: was introduced by Government of Karnataka on 2.3.2018, with the goal of providing Universal Health Coverage to all residents of the State.

evidence.quote: Basic Sum Assured is Rs. 5,00,000/- per Family, per annum for "Eligible Households (BPL)" and RSBY enrolled beneficiaries.

The integrated scheme covers Simple Secondary, Complex Secondary, Tertiary & Emergency Procedures.

flags.detail: Both sources are Government of Karnataka medical institute pages, not the scheme authority's (SAST) own page, which could not be reached. Undated; amounts may have changed since the scheme began in 2018. Confirm with SAST before review.

Wording differs slightly: one page says the scheme pays 30% of the package rate (up to Rs 1.5 lakh); the other says APL card holders pay 70% of the hospital bills. These appear consistent but use different bases (package rate vs hospital bill).

notes: BPL/APL card status is not asked in the questionnaire, so the level of cover is a manual check.
